set.body:
Raised by independent review during Epic 1/2 execution.

Problem

In the current architecture the spatial frame IS the metric: T_v = B D(W_v.) B^T. Once Epic 2 admits a general K, the support carries TWO objects - the frame row W_x. and the local metric K_x - and no epic states how they compose.

Candidates:
  (a) K_x replaces the weights entirely; the frame contributes only the support.
  (b) K_x is conjugated by the weights: K_x_eff = D(w_x)^(1/2) K_x D(w_x)^(1/2).
  (c) Weights are restricted to normalization bookkeeping and refused when a non-diagonal metric is present.

These give different numbers and different estimands. Epic 2 fixes a = w/sum(w) for the coherent covector, which presumes the frame still carries weights, but Epic 4 lowering says non-diagonal metrics take a support-streamed path without saying what happens to W.

Consequence that is already documented and will silently become false

README states: "Conservative normalization makes every feature distribute unit mass across overlapping measurements, so local total geometries sum to global geometry."

That conservation requires sum_x W_x. = 1 per feature, giving sum_x T_x = B B^T. Under per-support metrics it requires sum_x pad(K_x) = K_global. For local precisions K_x = Sigma_x^-1 this is false in general: a local precision is not the restriction of the global precision. The conservation law does not survive non-diagonal metrics.

Acceptance

- One declared composition rule for (frame weights, metric), with the other options refused rather than silently coerced.
- normalization = conservative either refuses a non-feature-additive metric or documents that conservation is a feature-additive-only capability.
- A conservation law test asserted only under the capability that guarantees it, and an explicit test that it is refused (not merely wrong) otherwise.
- README/vignette conservation claim gated the same way as the Epic 8 searchlight-cost claim.
set.title: Frame-metric composition is undefined; conservative conservation law breaks for non-diagonal metrics
